stimuli.title: The Lantern Maker's Apprentice
stimuli.mainTextMarkdown:
Inside Master Chen's narrow workshop, the air smelled of steamed cedar. Toby held his breath as he eased mulberry paper onto bamboo ribs.

'You grip the brush as though it might bolt,' Master Chen murmured. 'Paper remembers an anxious hand.'

Toby relaxed his shoulders and lifted the frame toward the window, catching a pale ghost of light until Master Chen tapped the rim: 'Almost straight—redo the third panel.'

stimuli.title: Mapping the Seafloor
stimuli.mainTextMarkdown: More than three-quarters of the ocean floor remains poorly {{gap:1}}. Because seawater blocks sunlight, satellite cameras cannot {{gap:2}} deep trenches. Instead, researchers {{gap:3}} on sonar pulses bounced from ships—a method that works, {{gap:4}} slowly.

stimuli.title: Magpie at Dawn
stimuli.mainTextMarkdown:
Before the sprinklers hiss awake,
A silver flute along the fence
Pours liquid notes no strings could make.
He cocks his head to read the turf
As scholars read a starry sky.

stimuli.title: Why Honeybees Dance in the Dark
stimuli.mainTextMarkdown: Worker bees move across wax combs in darkness, yet one scout guides nestmates straight to flowers kilometres away. {{gap:1}} Austrian zoologist Karl von Frisch discovered scouts perform a figure-of-eight dance. {{gap:2}} If flowers stood toward the sun, she waggled straight upward. {{gap:3}} Followers press antennae against her abdomen to read every turn.

extracts.label: A
extracts.bodyMarkdown: Its angle relative to gravity translated the sun's outdoor position onto the vertical comb.

extracts.label: B
extracts.bodyMarkdown: In this pitch-black hive, visual hand signals would obviously be useless.

extracts.label: C
extracts.bodyMarkdown: Surprisingly, bumblebees store far less winter honey than European honeybees.

extracts.label: D
extracts.bodyMarkdown: Because they cannot see in the dark, touch and sound carry the message.

extracts.label: A
extracts.title: Samira
extracts.bodyMarkdown: I built a solar water filter after floods turned tap water muddy. My early two-bucket rig leaked badly and looked dreadful, until my cousin taught me to test each seal separately.

extracts.label: B
extracts.title: Daniel
extracts.bodyMarkdown: Everyone built arcade games, so I deliberately built a plant-watering sensor. After it saved Gran's ferns during a heatwave, I decided every future project should help someone real.

extracts.label: C
extracts.title: Priya
extracts.bodyMarkdown: My bird-call counter started as a maths-assignment shortcut. It still works far better on quiet mornings than noisy lunchtimes, yet the local council asked to borrow our recordings.

extracts.label: D
extracts.title: Noah
extracts.bodyMarkdown: My brother and I argued carving wooden gears for a page-turner. Next time I'd test the rubber gripper on glossy books first and leave varnish until last.

stimuli.title: Welcome to Our School
stimuli.mainTextMarkdown: Three Year 5 students from another town join your school on Monday. Write an **advice sheet** titled *Welcome to Our School* helping them navigate their first week.

stimuli.title: Storm Blackout
stimuli.mainTextMarkdown: Your neighbourhood lost electricity for 24 hours in a storm (see visual stimulus). Write a **diary entry** reflecting on how the blackout changed your day.
